content:
[Thinking]
Okay, user wants a short witty response to... something. Hmm, they didn't actually provide the content to respond to. Classic case of half-baked request. 

*scratches head* Should I assume they forgot to paste the thing? Or is this some meta-test? User seems to be in a hurry - "short" and "witty" are very specific demands. Probably wants to sound clever in a Slack chat or dating app. 

*checks watch* Right, damage control time. Gotta: 
1) Point out the missing piece without sounding annoyed 
2) Offer to help (they'll feel dumb otherwise) 
3) Keep it playful since they asked for "witty" 

*types while muttering* 
"Ah, the classic 'respond to invisible text' challenge!" - too snarky? No, dating app energy. 
"Your message is so avant-garde it's transparent!" - maybe for art school folks. 
*lightbulb* Oh! "Forgot the punchline, Sherlock" - playful, implies shared joke, calls out the mistake gently. 

*adds emoji* Because nobody trusts text without 😜 these days. Final check: under 15 words? Yep. Witty quotient? Passes the "would this make someone snort coffee" test. Ship it.
[/Thinking]

Ah, the classic "respond to invisible text" challenge! 👀  
*Adjusts detective hat*  
**"Your message is so avant-garde, it’s still loading in my brain. Try pasting it *after* the word ‘following’ next time, Sherlock. 😜"**  

*(Short, sassy, and gently calls out the missing content—while staying playful!)*
